title: AI Search Ranking Factors: What's Documented, What's Measured, What's Guesswork
metaTitle: AI Search Ranking Factors: Documented vs Guessed
metaDescription: No AI engine publishes ranking factors. Every factor ranked by evidence: what engines document, what studies measured, and what is only guesswork.
shortAnswer: No AI engine publishes ranking factors, so every list mixes documented rules, study results and guesses. Documented: pages must be crawlable and indexed, and Google says original, non-commodity content matters most. Measured: cited statistics and quotations, third-party coverage, and fresh, well-structured pages. Guesswork: entity authority and backlinks. Fix access first, make claims specific and sourced second, earn mentions elsewhere third.
intro:
Most "AI search ranking factors" lists are SEO checklists with new labels, and they present guesses as facts. We sort every factor into three grades instead. **Documented** means an engine's own documentation says so. **Measured** means a published study found it, with limits we state. **Inference** means plausible but untested.

The grade matters because AI answers are close to winner-take-most. In [AEOeye's recommendation benchmark](/blog/ai-brand-recommendation-measurement) (127 audits, 892 answers; small and self-selected, not a market estimate), 71.4% of the 147 ranked brand mentions came first. Being named at all is the hard part, so put effort where the evidence is strongest. [Check whether AI names your brand](/) before you change anything.

sections.heading: What are the AI search ranking factors, ranked by evidence?
sections.body:
Ten factors come up in advice and research, ranked here by how far we trust them. Only the first two are documented by engines, three more are measured in studies, and the rest are mixed, inferred or contradicted. Nobody publishes weights, so the order is our judgment, not an algorithm.

| # | Factor | Grade | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Crawl and index access | Documented | OpenAI, Perplexity, Anthropic and Google docs |
| 2 | Original, non-commodity content | Documented (Google) | Google's AI guide: likely matters most |
| 3 | Specific, cited claims | Measured | GEO study: statistics, quotes, sources raised visibility |
| 4 | Third-party (earned) coverage | Measured | Toronto study: AI search leaned on earned media |
| 5 | Freshness and clear metadata | Measured, observational | GEO-16: strongest page-quality link to citation |
| 6 | Self-contained page structure | Mixed | Microsoft advises it; Google says chunking is unnecessary |
| 7 | Structured data | Mixed | Google: not needed; Microsoft: helps |
| 8 | Entity clarity | Inference | Consistent name, category, profile links |
| 9 | Backlinks | Inference | No AI-specific test found |
| 10 | llms.txt, keyword stuffing | Not supported | Google ignores llms.txt; stuffing did not help |

![A hand resting on a laptop trackpad while the screen shows a candlestick chart and printed charts lie on the desk.](https://images.pexels.com/photos/7567486/pexels-photo-7567486.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: Which AI search ranking factors do the engines document?
sections.body:
Engines document access rules, not ranking weights. OpenAI, Perplexity and Anthropic each say blocking their search crawler can keep you out of answers, and Google says a page must be indexed and snippet-eligible. Google adds that [unique, useful content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) will likely matter more than any other suggestion in its guide.

- **OpenAI:** [OAI-SearchBot](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots) surfaces sites in ChatGPT search. Opted-out sites are not shown in answers, though they can appear as navigational links. GPTBot, the training crawler, is a separate setting.
- **Perplexity:** [PerplexityBot](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots) surfaces and links sites in Perplexity search results. It is not used to train foundation models.
- **Anthropic:** disabling [Claude-SearchBot](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8896518-does-anthropic-crawl-data-from-the-web-and-how-can-site-owners-block-the-crawler) may reduce your visibility and accuracy in Claude search results.
- **Google:** AI Overviews and AI Mode [retrieve from the Search index and use query fan-out](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide). A page must be [indexed and snippet-eligible](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) to appear as a supporting link. Blocking [Google-Extended](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/google-common-crawlers) does not affect Search inclusion.

For most brands this gate is already open. In [AEOeye's crawler access study](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory) (October 2026; 391 well-known sites, a convenience sample), 1 of 193 SaaS sites blocked any AI retrieval bot in robots.txt, against 27 of 38 news publishers. But 24 of 88 e-commerce and consumer homepages challenged our self-identified crawler, so check firewall and CDN rules as well as robots.txt.

One more documented fact: Google says [no third-party tool has access to its internal ranking or AI systems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide). That includes ours. We measure outcomes, not weights.

sections.heading: Which AI search ranking factors does research support?
sections.body:
Three have published evidence: cited, specific claims; third-party coverage; and fresh, well-structured pages. Each study has limits that matter. Read them as evidence of direction, not weights you can drop into a spreadsheet.

**Specific, cited claims.** The [GEO study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735) (KDD 2024) built a 10,000-query benchmark (results on its 1,000-query test split) and a research engine using GPT-3.5-turbo and the top five Google results. Adding statistics, quotations or cited sources lifted a rewritten source's visibility by 30–40% on one metric and 15–30% on another; keyword stuffing gave little to none. On Perplexity.ai, quotation addition scored 29.1 on position-adjusted word count against a 24.1 baseline, and keyword stuffing 21.9. The limit: a simulated engine measuring share of an answer, not whether you get retrieved.

**Third-party coverage.** A [University of Toronto study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08919) (data collected August 2025) compared Google with a search-enabled GPT model. For US software-product queries, AI search cited 72.7% earned media and 26.7% brand-owned sites; Google showed 45.4% earned and 43.7% brand. In consumer-electronics queries it also leaned away from community platforms such as Reddit, which sits awkwardly with the popular claim that Reddit dominates AI citations. One engine, product-style queries: do not build a plan on this alone.

**Fresh, well-structured pages.** [GEO-16](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.10762) audited 1,100 URLs behind 1,702 citations from Brave Summary, Google AI Overviews and Perplexity for 70 product-intent prompts on B2B SaaS pages. Metadata and freshness correlated most with citation (r = 0.68), then semantic HTML (0.65) and structured data (0.63). The authors warn the design is observational and may be confounded.

![Angled close-up of a monitor showing a candlestick price chart with a blue trend line and green and red bars.](https://images.pexels.com/photos/38906370/pexels-photo-38906370.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: Which AI search ranking factors are educated guesses?
sections.body:
Entity authority and backlinks are the two big ones. Both are plausible, and we found no AI-specific test of either. Treat them as cheap hygiene, not levers you can promise results from.

- **Entity clarity.** A consistent name, category, description and profile links help machines tell you apart from lookalikes. Google says [Organization markup can help disambiguate your organization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/organization) in Search, but we found no evidence that answer engines weight it. Do it, because it takes an hour. See [what entity SEO is](/blog/what-is-entity-seo).
- **Backlinks.** Microsoft calls them [essential for discoverability](https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en/blog/post/october-2025/optimizing-your-content-for-inclusion-in-ai-search-answers), and Google's AI features sit on its core ranking systems, so links likely help indirectly. Unlinked mentions are a separate question, covered in [brand mentions vs backlinks](/blog/brand-mentions). Google warns that seeking inauthentic mentions is not as helpful as it seems.
- **Structured data.** Google says [structured data is not required](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) for generative AI search, while Microsoft recommends it. Write the visible text first, then add schema that matches it ([schema guide](/blog/structured-data-for-ai)).
- **llms.txt.** Google says it ignores the file. In our study, 173 of 330 checkable sites publish one. We publish one too, and we think it is [overrated as a lever](/blog/llms-txt-is-overrated).

Self-contained sections are the one place Microsoft and Google disagree: Microsoft describes Copilot breaking pages into smaller pieces, while Google says there is no need to chunk. We side with Google on not fragmenting pages and with Microsoft on writing sections that stand alone.

sections.heading: What should you prioritize?
sections.body:
Fix access, then make claims specific and sourced, then earn coverage where engines already look, then measure repeatedly. That order follows evidence strength, and the first two steps cost only time.

1. **Check the gate.** Unless you have a reason to block them, allow OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and Claude-SearchBot in robots.txt, check CDN and firewall logs for blocked bots, and confirm key pages are indexed. Our [AI robots.txt generator](/tools/ai-robots-txt-generator) writes the rules.
2. **Rewrite your ten most important pages with sourced specifics.** The passage-level method is in [what makes content quotable by AI](/answers/what-makes-content-quotable-by-ai).
3. **Find where your category's answers come from.** Ask engines your buyers' questions, list the third-party sources they cite, and earn honest coverage there. [How AI assistants choose brands](/blog/how-ai-assistants-choose-brands) explains the shortlist.
4. **Keep dates honest.** Update pages when facts change and show the update date.
5. **Measure more than once.** [Research on AI search measurement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07585) finds answers vary across runs, prompts and time, so a single answer is an anecdote.

![Two hands holding a silver trophy up against a clear blue sky.](https://images.pexels.com/photos/6412253/pexels-photo-6412253.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

AEOeye's free audit asks three buyer questions on ChatGPT live and shows who is named instead of you. The $29 report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity and ten questions. For daily monitoring across hundreds of prompts, dedicated trackers such as Profound, Peec AI or Otterly do that; we do not.

keyTakeaways: No engine publishes ranking weights; sort every claim into documented, measured or guessed before acting on it.
Access is the only gate documented by OpenAI, Perplexity, Anthropic and Google, and our data says most brands pass it.
Measured levers are specific, cited claims, third-party coverage and fresh, well-structured pages, each with study limits.
Entity authority, backlinks, schema and llms.txt are inference or contested; do them cheaply and do not promise results.

faqs.q: Is there an official list of AI search ranking factors?
faqs.a: No. Google, OpenAI, Perplexity and Anthropic document crawler access and, in Google's case, content quality principles, but none publishes ranking weights. Any list that gives percentages is an estimate. Google also says no third-party tool can see its internal ranking or AI systems, so treat precise-looking scores with suspicion.

faqs.q: Do ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI use the same factors?
faqs.a: Only partly. All three need to fetch your page, and each documents its own crawler. Beyond that they differ: the Toronto study found engines differ in domain diversity and freshness, and Google's AI features draw on its Search index. Test the same buyer questions on each engine rather than assuming one result transfers.

faqs.q: Do backlinks still matter for AI search?
faqs.a: Probably indirectly. Google's AI features sit on its core ranking systems, and Microsoft calls backlinks essential for discoverability. We found no study that isolates links as a factor in which sources AI answers cite. Unlinked mentions on trusted third-party sites are a separate and better-supported route.

faqs.q: Will llms.txt or schema markup get me cited?
faqs.a: Not on their own. Google says it ignores llms.txt and that no special schema is needed for its AI features. Microsoft recommends schema, and one observational study linked structured data to citation, so keep markup that matches your visible text. Neither replaces content specific enough to quote.

faqs.q: How do I find out which factor is holding me back?
faqs.a: Start with the gate: robots.txt, firewall logs and indexing. Then run the same buyer questions several times on each engine and read which sources get cited instead of you. If the gate is open and rivals win on third-party sources, coverage is the gap; if they win on specifics, rewrite your pages.

definitions.definition: A technique that has a language model fetch relevant documents at answer time and use them to generate its response, instead of relying only on what it memorized in training.
Google's term for a set of concurrent, related searches the model generates from one question to pull in more supporting pages before it writes an answer.
Work aimed at improving how often and how prominently a source appears in AI-generated answers; the term comes from the 2023 research paper of the same name.
